i.296444294:
LPH arrived to begin the annual electrical system check. Upon arrival, no immediate electrical concerns were presented prior to our electrical inspection. 

We began our evaluation at the main electrical/distribution panel. This is where we assessed the internal conditions, age, connections and voltage readings. During this inspection, all of the inspected parameters meet the required threshold for a healthy panel. However, there are a few recommendations we assessed during this inspection. 

First we discovered that there two sets of breakers that are apart of a shared neutral circuit. A specific type of breaker would need to be installed in their place to properly protect this circuit and any personnel who needs to work on this circuit. Lastly, there’s no system put in place to protect appliances/electronics from spikes of electric which target the sensitive components inside these units. A whole home surge protection device is recommended if the homeowners were interested in  protecting their main utility equipment with a one time investment unit.

Next, we inspected all of the protective systems for personnel and equipment in the home such as the smoke detectors, GFI protection devices, and the grounding system. First, we discovered that the water and gas meter does not meet today’s grounding standards to protect against any leakage of electricity from traveling on the pipes. The next was confirmation that all of the existing smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors are up-to-date. However, we identified two bedroom locations that do not have active smoke detectors. Lastly, we identified two junction boxes that do not have the any covers installed and two sets of open splices that have been taped for the lighting above the workshop area. All other devices in the home were tested and functioning properly prior to leaving today.

We provided options to remedy all of our electrical recommendations, which was presented today. All of the options that were not approved will be emailed along with the electrical evaluation form and invoice for today’s visit. We thank you for allowing us in your home to service you and we look forward to servicing you in the future.

e.438328499:
As we approach the winter months and the start of flu season, maintaining healthy indoor air quality becomes increasingly important. With windows and doors remaining closed more frequently and heating systems running regularly, airborne particles and other contaminants can circulate throughout your home.

LPH recommends considering the following indoor air quality upgrades to help improve air filtration, reduce certain airborne contaminants, and support a cleaner, healthier indoor environment.

1. UV Air Purification Light

A UV air purification light is installed within your home’s HVAC system and uses ultraviolet light technology to help reduce certain airborne microorganisms as air circulates through the system. This technology can help support improved indoor air quality and provide an additional layer of protection against certain biological contaminants.

2. Electric Air Cleaner with Upgraded Filtration

An electric air cleaner with upgraded filtration is designed to capture airborne particles, including dust, pollen, and other common indoor particulates. By enhancing your HVAC system’s filtration capabilities, this upgrade can help improve indoor air quality, reduce particle circulation, and keep internal HVAC components cleaner.

Why Consider These Upgrades?

During the heating season, your HVAC system plays an important role in circulating and filtering the air throughout your home. Improving your system’s air purification and filtration capabilities can provide several benefits:

* Help reduce certain airborne contaminants and microorganisms.
* Capture more airborne particles, including dust and pollen.
* Support cleaner air circulation throughout your home.
* Help keep HVAC system components cleaner.
* Improve overall indoor comfort and air quality.

Prepare Your Home for the Winter Season

LPH encourages homeowners to explore these indoor air quality solutions before the heating season gets underway. Investing in enhanced air purification and filtration can be a proactive step toward maintaining a cleaner and more comfortable home environment throughout the winter months.

For more information about these upgrades and to determine which option may be best suited for your home’s HVAC system, contact LPH. We’re happy to help you make an informed decision about your indoor air quality needs.

i.331202541:
LPH arrived to begin the annual electrical system check. Upon arrival, no immediate concerns or presented prior to our electrical inspection. However, the homeowners just wanted to ensure that we’re still being thorough during our electrical inspection. 

We began our evaluation at the main electrical/distribution panel. This is where we assessed the internal conditions, age, connections and voltage readings. During this inspection, all of the inspected parameters meet the required threshold for a healthy panel.

Next, we inspected all of the protective systems for personnel and equipment in the home such as the smoke detectors, GFI protection devices, and the grounding system. First, we discovered that the water and gas meter does meet today’s grounding standards to protect against any leakage of electricity from traveling on the pipes. The next was confirmation that all of the existing smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors are installed in the right locations and up-to-date. Thirdly, we identified that main bathroom exhaust fan in the second floor bathroom, was pretty loud, which indicates that this unit is starting to fail internally. We identify that all the other bathroom exhaust fans in the home are the same age and style, which indicates that these units are probably not too far behind in terms of failure. Lastly, we identified two GFI outlets on the front and back portion of the home that no longer contain their safety features, the two additional GFI‘s (one being in the garden, and one underneath the exhaust pipe) are very old in age, and struggling to respond when tested. The last GFI, that is apart of the lamp post circuit is functioning correctly. However, in addition to most of these GFI’s either not functioning or being very old and slow to respond, they’re missing the proper exterior covers require required to protect against weather elements.  All other devices in the home were tested and functioning properly prior to leaving today.

We provided options to remedy all of our electrical recommendations, which was presented today. All of the options that were not approved will be emailed along with the electrical evaluation form and invoice for today’s visit. We thank you for allowing us in your home to service you and we look forward to servicing you in the future.

During today’s electrical system check, LPH performed an evaluation of the home’s electrical system, including the electrical panel, breakers, internal connections, switches, receptacles, and accessible electrical devices throughout the home. We also evaluated the condition of the existing devices, checked for loose connections, signs of overheating, electrical arcing, physical damage, and general wear and deterioration. Exterior electrical devices and their protection against weather exposure and moisture intrusion were also reviewed.

During our inspection, LPH identified significant deterioration among the existing switches and receptacles. These devices are approximately 30 years old and have reached a point where multiple devices are showing signs of failure. We found cracked plastic housings, weakened connections, wiring slipping out of devices, and evidence of electrical arcing. Almost every electrical box we opened and inspected showed some degree of deterioration or connection concerns.

Before making any recommendations, we went over our findings directly with the homeowners and physically showed them the damaged devices and the conditions we discovered during the inspection. We explained how these devices deteriorate over time, why loose connections and electrical arcing are concerning, and the potential for overheating and electrical failure if these conditions are allowed to continue.

Recommendations & Options Reviewed With Homeowners:

1. Whole-Home Device Restoration: LPH recommended replacing all switches and receptacles throughout the home. Since these devices were installed around the same time, the widespread deterioration indicates that similar issues can reasonably be expected in devices that have not yet been inspected or are not currently showing symptoms. Replacing everything together provides a comprehensive restoration rather than waiting for individual devices to fail. This option also includes a dimmer switch and two GFCI receptacles as an added value.
2. Partial Home Device Replacement: An alternative option was provided to replace up to 50 switches and receptacles, allowing the homeowners to prioritize the most deteriorated devices while addressing a significant portion of the identified concerns.
3. Exterior Device & Weatherproofing Upgrades: As part of the device replacement options, LPH also included upgrading applicable exterior receptacles to weather-resistant devices, installing two weather-resistant GFCI receptacles, adding exterior in-use bubble covers to protect receptacles from direct rain and moisture exposure, and sealing exterior electrical enclosures with silicone to help prevent water intrusion.

We explained the importance of addressing these conditions proactively, especially considering the age of the devices and the widespread deterioration already identified. Continuing to operate with damaged devices and compromised connections increases the potential for additional arcing, overheating, and electrical failures.

At this time, the homeowners will be sent the estimates along with today’s electrical system evaluation for their review and consideration. They can take the time to review the available options and determine how they would like to proceed.

Thank you for allowing LPH into your home. It was a pleasure meeting with you, and we appreciate the opportunity to evaluate your electrical system.

LPH recommends replacing all switches and receptacles throughout the home. During today’s inspection, we found that the existing devices are approximately 30 years old and have deteriorated significantly from normal use and age. Multiple devices were found with cracked plastic housings, weakened wire connections, and wiring beginning to slip out of the devices. Evidence of electrical arcing was also identified.

After inspecting multiple locations throughout the home, it became apparent that these issues are not isolated to one or two devices. Nearly every electrical box inspected showed some degree of deterioration or connection concerns.

Because these devices were all installed around the same time, it is reasonable to expect similar wear throughout the remainder of the home, including locations that have not yet shown obvious symptoms. Continuing to operate with deteriorating devices increases the potential for electrical arcing, overheating, and eventual electrical failure.

LPH strongly recommends proactively replacing all switches and receptacles throughout the home rather than addressing individual failures as they occur. This provides the homeowner with refreshed, secure electrical connections throughout the home and helps reduce the risk of future connection-related issues.

As an added value with this upgrade, LPH will include one dimmer switch and two GFCI receptacles at no additional charge.

Premium Whole-Home Surge Protection
LPH will install a premium whole-home surge protection device at the home’s main electrical panel. This device is designed to protect the home’s electrical system and connected equipment from damaging voltage spikes and transient surges before they can travel throughout the home’s wiring.
Many homeowners think of lightning when they hear the term “surge,” but the majority of power surges actually originate inside the home. Everyday appliances such as air conditioners, refrigerators, heat pumps, furnaces, microwaves, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and even garage door openers create small electrical surges—known as microsurges—every time their motors cycle on and off. While each individual surge is small, thousands of these microsurges occur over time and gradually wear down the sensitive electronic components found in today’s modern appliances and equipment.
Whole-home surge protection helps absorb and divert these surges away from the home’s electrical system, reducing cumulative damage to expensive electronics and appliances. This is especially important in newer homes, where nearly every major appliance contains sophisticated circuit boards and microprocessors that are far more sensitive to voltage fluctuations than older equipment.
In addition to protecting against internally generated microsurges, whole-home surge protection also provides a critical first line of defense against larger surges originating from the utility company, switching events on the electrical grid, nearby lightning strikes, or power being restored after an outage.
Benefits of premium whole-home surge protection include:
	• Protects HVAC systems, refrigerators, ovens, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and other major appliances.
	• Helps safeguard sensitive electronics such as televisions, computers, gaming systems, networking equipment, and smart home devices.
	• Reduces the long-term effects of everyday microsurges that slowly degrade electronic components.
	• Can help extend the service life of modern appliances and equipment by reducing electrical stress on internal circuit boards.
	• Helps minimize the likelihood of costly repairs or premature equipment replacement due to surge damage.
	• Provides continuous protection for the entire home’s electrical system without relying solely on individual plug-in surge strips.
	• Offers added peace of mind during storms, utility switching events, and unexpected power outages.
As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

Premium Surge Protection Warranty & Replacement Coverage

The installed surge protection device also provides additional protection beyond the device itself. If the surge protector is ever sacrificed or fails as a result of a covered surge event, the device is backed by a lifetime warranty and coverage of up to $100,000 toward covered damage to the home’s electrical components and connected equipment, subject to the manufacturer’s warranty terms and conditions.

If the surge protector ever needs to be replaced under the warranty, the replacement device is provided at no charge. LPH will also handle the replacement installation for a $150 labor charge, helping make future warranty replacement straightforward and affordable for the homeowner.

This means the homeowner is not simply purchasing a surge protector—they are adding a long-term layer of protection to the home’s electrical system while also having manufacturer-backed coverage in the event of a significant surge.

As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

i.339779140:
LPH returned today to complete the recommended electrical service replacement following the previous evaluation, which identified extensive water intrusion, corrosion, and moisture-related deterioration throughout the existing exterior meter base and interior electrical panel.

The existing water-affected service equipment was removed and replaced with a new electrical service assembly. This included installation of a new exterior meter base, emergency disconnect, conduit, and associated service wiring. New four-wire conductors were installed between the exterior disconnect and interior panel, allowing the interior panel to be properly reconfigured as a subpanel with the required separation of neutrals and grounds. The grounding and bonding systems were also addressed as part of the replacement, including the required bonding bridge and grounding connections.

All new grounding connections were established at the new exterior emergency disconnect. The existing grounding conductors were relocated from the interior panel to the new service disconnect, where the grounding system is now properly established. An additional grounding connection was also installed to the home’s metal water piping, providing the necessary supplementary grounding and bonding required by applicable electrical code.

A new 42-space Eaton CH electrical loadcenter was installed to replace the existing moisture-damaged panel. Upon performing a thorough evaluation of the homes main electrical service I found no major discrepancies, however I had one substantial estimate for the homeowners at the time of our check today. The one recommendation I had was regarding the main breaker panel. The panel appears to be in the end stages of progressive corrosion. I analyzed substantial rust on not only the panel housing but some segments of wiring as well. Most of the panels bare copper/ aluminum exhibit signs of oxidization or corrosion from moisture exposure over the span of 50+ years.  The panel has eclipsed what we would deem to be the average life expectancy for breaker panels. The panel is 50 years old now. As panels age, the safety features within their breakers can begin to fail to function in the event of an electrical fault. We lose the ability to be able to gauge proper function of these breakers as they age until sometimes, we lose power entirely. Separate from this, should any breakers fail, or need to be replaced, it can be difficult to find replacements as they do not manufacture these parts anymore. Primarily the main breakers are the cause of concern. If the main breaker were to trip for any reason, there is a strong likelihood it would not reset, as it is not considered a “serviceable” breaker. The rest of the homes equipment appears to be in good condition with no other signs of potential failure. For all of the reasons listed above, I have provided a sole estimate today to replace the main breaker panel. Should you have any questions or concerns regarding todays visit or our findings, please do not hesitate to contact us. Thank you for having me out today and I look forward to our next visit!

LPH reviewed the findings and recommendations with the homeowner, and all of the above-listed work was approved, completed, and tested today. The two 20-amp breakers, three duplex receptacles, kitchen GFCI receptacle, and ceiling fan remote receiver assembly were replaced.

We discovered that there’s no system put in place to protect appliances/electronics from spikes of electric which target the sensitive components inside these units. A whole home surge protection device is recommended if the homeowners were interested in  protecting their main utility equipment with a one time investment unit. This main electrical/distribution panel is also maxed out and most newer circuit or electrical equipment could not be installed within this existing panel

Next, we inspected all of the protective systems for personnel and equipment in the home such as the smoke detectors, GFI protection devices, and the grounding system. First, we discovered that the water and gas meter does not meet today’s grounding standards to protect against any leakage of electricity from traveling on the pipes. The next was confirmation that all of the existing smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors are installed in the right locations. However, we discovered that the existing units are past their 10 lifespan, and we recommend them to be replaced asap. All other devices in the home were tested and functioning properly prior to leaving today.

We provided options to remedy all of our electrical recommendations, which was presented today. The standard electrical package was approved by Matt and was partially completed today. We installed two brand new single pole switches in the master bedroom to replace the existing units that were failed/broken. We will return to rough in the new homeowner supplied light fixture on the staircase wall at a later date. The new switches were tested and working properly prior to leaving today.All of the options that were not approved will be emailed along with the electrical evaluation form and invoice for today’s visit. During today’s electrical system check, LPH performed a thorough evaluation of the home’s electrical system. This included inspecting the electrical panel, breakers, internal connections, grounding and bonding, and overall condition of the electrical service. We also checked receptacles and switches throughout the home, verified proper operation, looked for loose connections, signs of overheating, arcing, corrosion, and physical damage, and evaluated GFCI protection in the areas where required. We also reviewed the exterior electrical devices for proper weather protection and checked the smoke alarm protection throughout the home.

Summary of Findings & Recommendations:

During our evaluation, LPH identified the following items that we reviewed with the homeowner and provided options for:

1. Exterior Receptacles: Three exterior receptacles were identified for replacement with weather-resistant GFCI devices. Two existing devices are showing internal corrosion, while the third receptacle serving the outdoor hot tub is currently neither GFCI-protected nor weather-rated. LPH recommends replacing all three, properly mounting them to their electrical boxes, and sealing around the exterior to help prevent moisture intrusion.
2. Smoke Alarm: LPH recommends installing a new 10-year sealed-lithium-battery smoke alarm in the hallway outside the bedrooms to provide reliable smoke detection without the need for routine battery replacements.
3. Premium Whole-Home Surge Protection: LPH recommends installing our premium whole-home surge protection device at the electrical panel. This provides an additional layer of protection against damaging voltage spikes and surges that can affect sensitive electronics, appliances, and HVAC equipment throughout the home.
4. Bathroom Switch & Wiring Correction: LPH identified an existing bathroom switch that is arcing and should be replaced. Since the bathroom heater is no longer being used, LPH recommended removing the heater wiring from the switch configuration and installing a new twin single-pole switch to independently operate the fan and lighting. We also identified an improper wiring arrangement at the bathroom fan where the equipment grounding conductor was being used as a neutral due to insufficient conductors. LPH recommended correcting this wiring so the neutral is returned to its intended function and the equipment grounding conductor is properly reconnected.

Work Approved & Completed Today:

The homeowner elected to move forward with the bathroom wiring correction at this time. LPH completed the wiring repair, corrected the improper use of the grounding conductor, restored the neutral to its intended function, and properly reconnected the equipment ground. The bathroom fan and lighting controls were tested following the repair and confirmed to be functioning properly.

The remaining recommendations were reviewed with the homeowner for future consideration.

Today’s work was completed and tested. The invoice summary will be emailed to the homeowner for their records.

e.438394061:
Premium Whole-Home Surge Protection
LPH will install a premium whole-home surge protection device at the home’s main electrical panel. This device is designed to protect the home’s electrical system and connected equipment from damaging voltage spikes and transient surges before they can travel throughout the home’s wiring.
Many homeowners think of lightning when they hear the term “surge,” but the majority of power surges actually originate inside the home. Everyday appliances such as air conditioners, refrigerators, heat pumps, furnaces, microwaves, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and even garage door openers create small electrical surges—known as microsurges—every time their motors cycle on and off. While each individual surge is small, thousands of these microsurges occur over time and gradually wear down the sensitive electronic components found in today’s modern appliances and equipment.
Whole-home surge protection helps absorb and divert these surges away from the home’s electrical system, reducing cumulative damage to expensive electronics and appliances. This is especially important in newer homes, where nearly every major appliance contains sophisticated circuit boards and microprocessors that are far more sensitive to voltage fluctuations than older equipment.
In addition to protecting against internally generated microsurges, whole-home surge protection also provides a critical first line of defense against larger surges originating from the utility company, switching events on the electrical grid, nearby lightning strikes, or power being restored after an outage.
Benefits of premium whole-home surge protection include:
	• Protects HVAC systems, refrigerators, ovens, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and other major appliances.
	• Helps safeguard sensitive electronics such as televisions, computers, gaming systems, networking equipment, and smart home devices.
	• Reduces the long-term effects of everyday microsurges that slowly degrade electronic components.
	• Can help extend the service life of modern appliances and equipment by reducing electrical stress on internal circuit boards.
	• Helps minimize the likelihood of costly repairs or premature equipment replacement due to surge damage.
	• Provides continuous protection for the entire home’s electrical system without relying solely on individual plug-in surge strips.
	• Offers added peace of mind during storms, utility switching events, and unexpected power outages.
As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

Premium Surge Protection Warranty & Replacement Coverage

The installed surge protection device also provides additional protection beyond the device itself. If the surge protector is ever sacrificed or fails as a result of a covered surge event, the device is backed by a lifetime warranty and coverage of up to $100,000 toward covered damage to the home’s electrical components and connected equipment, subject to the manufacturer’s warranty terms and conditions.

If the surge protector ever needs to be replaced under the warranty, the replacement device is provided at no charge. LPH will also handle the replacement installation for a $150 labor charge, helping make future warranty replacement straightforward and affordable for the homeowner.

This means the homeowner is not simply purchasing a surge protector—they are adding a long-term layer of protection to the home’s electrical system while also having manufacturer-backed coverage in the event of a significant surge.

As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

i.436935470:
Heating System Inspection Findings & Recommendations

LPH completed a heating system inspection on the approximately 20-year-old standard gas furnace. At the time of inspection, the furnace was operational and producing heat. However, I identified several concerns worth addressing as we head into the heating season.

Inspection Findings:

1. System Efficiency: The furnace is currently operating at approximately 79% efficiency. While the system is still functioning, this efficiency level is not ideal compared to newer, more energy-efficient equipment. Replacing the system could provide improved efficiency and potentially lower energy costs.
2. System Cleaning: The furnace was found to be dirty. LPH recommends performing a professional system cleaning to help improve airflow, maintain proper system performance, and reduce the risk of premature component failure.
3. UV Bulb Replacement: The UV light bulbs are due for replacement. The manufacturer recommends replacing these bulbs every two years to maintain optimal performance.
4. Heat Exchanger Condition: During the inspection, I observed a significant amount of rust on the heat exchanger. Over time, corrosion can worsen and potentially lead to cracks or holes in the heat exchanger. If this occurs, the furnace could become unsafe to operate and may need to be shut down.

Recommendations:

LPH recommends addressing the maintenance items, including a professional furnace cleaning and UV bulb replacement. Additionally, due to the system’s age, current efficiency, and visible rust on the heat exchanger, we strongly recommend scheduling a Comfort Consultant to evaluate the system and provide replacement options.

With a 20-year-old furnace heading into another heating season, it’s important to consider the reliability of the equipment and the potential for unexpected breakdowns.

Overall Assessment:

The furnace is currently operational; however, given its age and the concerns identified during the inspection, LPH recommends considering replacement rather than continuing to invest in an aging system. Our goal is to help ensure you have a safe, reliable, and efficient heating system to get you through the upcoming winter.

According to Rinnai technical support, error code 71 indicates a solenoid valve circuit failure or a potential control board failure. Moisture inside the unit can sometimes contribute to these issues. During further inspection of the bypass tee, technician identified that the water leak was originating from the elbow connected to the heat exchanger.

Performed triple system checks on 3 20+ year old Payne, Bryant, and Carrier gas furnaces. At this time 1/3 of the units are operating properly and within spec. It should be duly noted that all three units are showing their age, however. The units for both the “break room” and “office” are both off at this time due to concerns about heat exchanger integrity and burning safety. 

The unit (Carrier) for the breakroom has what appears to be severe rusting on the outside of the primary heat exchanger. Given this is a horizontal application, it is unlikely that the evaporator coil is dripping onto the heat exchanger and causing exterior rust. Instead, it is my worry that the heat exchanger is rusting from the inside out. This is a safety concern. The unit is burning “cleanly” but any leakage on the heat exchanger will release CO into the conditioned space (which is bad). 

The unit covering the front offices has excessive CO coming off of the flue (>400 ppm air free). Due to this, it is shutoff. Though the integrity of the heat exchanger appears to be solid, the excessively high CO could cause a catastrophic problem if it were to develop a crack, and it is against code to keep it running at current combustion readings. Additionally, the gas valve appears to have gone bad as it is not holding steady pressure. This is probably unrelated to the high CO present in the flue; however, it is not helping and would be a pricey repair on a 20+ year old unit (if possible). 

I will be strongly recommending replacing both units for the breakroom and office, and would like to discuss finding on the warehouse unit with management. Additionally, I will be providing options to replace the UV lights for both the office and breakroom systems. If we do go with repair (please don’t), all furnaces would need in depth cleanings. Assuming we’re going to peruse replacement, I will write an option just to clean the unit in the warehouse. 

That being said, the work that was performed today involved changing all premium filters on the units and cleaning the evaporator coil on the warehouse unit. Additionally Larry spoke to me about the energy bill for the summer. Though I did not check the outdoor coils today, nothing I could see on the heating side of things appear to be causing higher energy consumption. My recommendation would be to reevaluate the cooling systems before summer proper starts to make sure they’re ready to go and no surprises have appeared from the last time they were check until now.

Clothes and towels can feel softer, look brighter, and experience less mineral-related stiffness.
3. Easier cleaning
Less soap scum and mineral residue means less scrubbing in showers, tubs, and sinks.

7. Longer appliance lifespan
Reducing scale can help appliances operate more efficiently and potentially last longer.
8. Better plumbing protection
Helps reduce mineral scale accumulation inside pipes, valves, and fixtures.

Helps reduce cloudy spots and mineral film on dishes and drinking glasses.

i.437528765: This afternoon I arrived at the Walker family home to perform their annual electrical system and safety check. Upon my arrival Mr. Walker informed me he had a few items in the home he would like me to look at including switches, and a smoke detector. I identified that both a single pole switch, as well as a dimmer in the home were faulty and not working properly. I identified that the single pole switch controlling the garbage disposal was actually broken due to both age, as well as the back stabbed wiring method. I provided an estimate to replace both of the faulty switches, one being a dimmer, and restored full function to the affected fixtures. As for the detector, Mr. Walker showed me to a low voltage security system detector that he believed may not have been working in the basement, after asking a handful of questions we concluded that in fact none of the detectors were, or have worked, since the Walkers moved into the home. The reason for this conclusion is that the Walkers never assumed the contract for the security system, and were not actively paying, nor members of the provider. Mrs. Walker informed me that she also doesn’t believe the company is even still around. For the above listed reasons I have provided an estimate to add all detectors as required by code throughout the home. All of the other systems in the home appeared to be functioning properly and good condition at this time. If you have any questions or concerns please do not hesitate to reach out. Thank you for having us out today and I look forward to our next visit!

Came out today for a no heat on a 13 year old Amana. We had installed a new AC with new Honeywell communicating thermostat, and tenant believed that was the problem. Upon arrival, thermostat was blank. Found that the furnace control board was errored out on a blown fuse or flame rollout code. Flame rollout was tripped and upon reset furnace started back up. All thermostat connections were proper and thermostat operates properly when flame rollout was reset. 

Did a thorough visual inspection of the unit and all components that may have attributed to flame rollout. Performed a heating system check and found several areas of concerns with the heat exchanger. Ultimately we had way greater than 400 ppm of CO coming off of the flue so I condemned the heat exchanger. Talked to Sean about replacing the heat exchanger or getting the unit replaced. Sean elected to have a comfort consultant come out today so that he could make a decision on whether he will replace or repair. 

Please refer to system evaluation form for pictures and measurements taken. 

Waiving dispatch fee for this visit.

As part of the inspection, the technician thoroughly cleaned all drain overflows, including the bathtub and bathroom vanity, to eliminate the possibility of odor coming from buildup within the overflows. The technician then asked the homeowner not to run any water while monitoring the water meter for approximately 30 minutes. Out to home today for the yearly plumbing inspection. Upon arrival to home, there was only one concern to note. They have noticed that there is moisture buildup behind the current water softener system. Evaluated unit and found system to dripping from discharge piping when on standby mode. Due to age of system, suggested best solution is to replace the water treatment system. In the meantime, unplugged the unit and bypassed the softener to prevent further leakage. 

From there, performed full home plumbing inspection today. Inspected and evaluated 11 year old water heater system. Observed corrosion and moisture at the cold side inlet to the system. System is within the end of its average lifespan of 8-12 years. Due to current issues and age of system, suggested replacement to prevent further leakage and reliable hot water. Performed water quality test and found high hardness and chlorine in the water. For both major contaminants, suggested installation of our CitySoft Water filtration system to remove both hardness and chlorine through use of its dual-bed system. Lastly, tested water pressure to verify a safe threshold inside the home. 

Only other concern found during today’s evaluation has to do with the kitchen faucet. Found that the faucet is coming loose and no longer swivels at the base as intended. Current faucet is also extremely low-end. Suggested replacement for a higher quality moen faucet. Provided options for replacement of fixture in both pull-out and pull-down spray units. 

Went over recommendations with homeowners relatives who were onsite today. Emailed all recommendations to homeowners. Pricing provided today is valid for 60 days. If there are any questions about our recommendations, please reach out to our office. Thank you for trusting LPH.

There was also reports of water on the floor happening for some time. Upon inspection of the furnace I found significant rusting in the blower and burner compartments. Blower capacitor was in spec, and the blower was free spinning and receiving voltage, but wouldn’t turn under power. The initial issue was identified as a failed blower motor.

The heat exchanger is darkened, rusted, and shows signs of excessive water damage inside. I tested gas pressure to the burners and it was at the manufacturer’s specification. This would all indicate a significant airflow issue in the system, which cannot be fully tested without a working blower motor. 

We went over repair options and our team will be out this afternoon to review replacement options.

While reviewing their existing heat pump, we discussed that the dual capacitor is nearing the limits of its operating specifications. I explained that if the capacitor fails, it could prevent the heat pump from starting and operating properly while they are away, potentially leaving the home without heat.

At this time, the homeowners are primarily interested in gathering pricing for a future system replacement. I reviewed the benefits of upgrading to a new system, including improved energy efficiency, all-new equipment, a 10-year parts warranty, and a 10-year labor warranty. We also discussed the benefits of a Wi-Fi thermostat, which would allow them to remotely monitor and control their HVAC system while they are in Florida, providing additional peace of mind.

After reviewing everything, the homeowners decided they would prefer to hold off on replacing the system for now and requested that all options be emailed over for their review.

I left my business card with my contact information and encouraged them to call or text me with any questions or concerns.

Thank you again for allowing me into your home today and giving me the opportunity to go over your HVAC replacement options. I look forward to working with you when the time is right.

During today’s evaluation, we identified an opportunity to improve the circuit separation for the sump pump and water softener. Both appliances were currently spliced into the living room GFCI circuit through a junction box located beside the electrical panel. * Garage GFCI Protection: Install a new GFCI receptacle in the garage to provide additional protection against electrical shock.
* Whole-Home Surge Protection: Install a whole-home surge protection device at the electrical panel to help protect appliances, electronics, and sensitive equipment from damaging voltage spikes caused by utility fluctuations, lightning, and everyday operation of larger electrical equipment.

LPH will install a premium whole-home surge protection device at the home’s main electrical panel. This device is designed to protect the home’s electrical system and connected equipment from damaging voltage spikes and transient surges before they can travel throughout the home’s wiring.
Many homeowners think of lightning when they hear the term “surge,” but the majority of power surges actually originate inside the home. Everyday appliances such as air conditioners, refrigerators, heat pumps, furnaces, microwaves, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and even garage door openers create small electrical surges—known as microsurges—every time their motors cycle on and off. While each individual surge is small, thousands of these microsurges occur over time and gradually wear down the sensitive electronic components found in today’s modern appliances and equipment.
Whole-home surge protection helps absorb and divert these surges away from the home’s electrical system, reducing cumulative damage to expensive electronics and appliances. This is especially important in newer homes, where nearly every major appliance contains sophisticated circuit boards and microprocessors that are far more sensitive to voltage fluctuations than older equipment.
In addition to protecting against internally generated microsurges, whole-home surge protection also provides a critical first line of defense against larger surges originating from the utility company, switching events on the electrical grid, nearby lightning strikes, or power being restored after an outage.
Benefits of premium whole-home surge protection include:
	• Protects HVAC systems, refrigerators, ovens, dishwashers, washers, dryers, and other major appliances.
	• Helps safeguard sensitive electronics such as televisions, computers, gaming systems, networking equipment, and smart home devices.
	• Reduces the long-term effects of everyday microsurges that slowly degrade electronic components.
	• Can help extend the service life of modern appliances and equipment by reducing electrical stress on internal circuit boards.
	• Helps minimize the likelihood of costly repairs or premature equipment replacement due to surge damage.
	• Provides continuous protection for the entire home’s electrical system without relying solely on individual plug-in surge strips.
	• Offers added peace of mind during storms, utility switching events, and unexpected power outages.
As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

Premium Surge Protection Warranty & Replacement Coverage

The installed surge protection device also provides additional protection beyond the device itself. If the surge protector is ever sacrificed or fails as a result of a covered surge event, the device is backed by a lifetime warranty and coverage of up to $100,000 toward covered damage to the home’s electrical components and connected equipment, subject to the manufacturer’s warranty terms and conditions.

If the surge protector ever needs to be replaced under the warranty, the replacement device is provided at no charge. LPH will also handle the replacement installation for a $150 labor charge, helping make future warranty replacement straightforward and affordable for the homeowner.

This means the homeowner is not simply purchasing a surge protector—they are adding a long-term layer of protection to the home’s electrical system while also having manufacturer-backed coverage in the event of a significant surge.

As homes continue to rely on more connected technology and electronically controlled appliances, whole-home surge protection has become one of the most valuable upgrades for preserving the reliability, longevity, and performance of a home’s electrical equipment.

We also reviewed the overall condition and age of the existing electrical equipment and discussed potential improvements to the home’s electrical safety, reliability, and functionality.

GFCI Protection & Electrical Safety

We reviewed several areas throughout the home where GFCI protection is important, particularly the kitchen countertop receptacles, as well as other locations such as the washing machine receptacle and other areas where protection is required. GFCI devices are designed to quickly interrupt power when they detect an electrical current imbalance, helping reduce the risk of electrical shock, especially in areas where water and electricity may come into contact.

Exterior Receptacles & Weather Protection

We discussed the importance of having properly weather-rated electrical devices and enclosures at all exterior locations. One existing exterior GFCI located on the outside wall of the garage was found tripped, with evidence of water intrusion being a concern. The existing gray exterior cover is not properly rated for the exposed location and does not provide the necessary protection against direct weather exposure. Proper weather-resistant GFCI devices and appropriately rated in-use covers help protect electrical connections from rain and moisture, reducing the potential for corrosion, nuisance tripping, and premature device failure.

Back-Stabbed Electrical Devices

We also reviewed locations throughout the home where receptacles and switches were originally wired using the back-stab connection method. These connections rely on internal spring tension to hold the wiring in place rather than the more secure screw-terminal connections. Over time, these connections can lose their holding tension, potentially allowing wires to loosen. Loose connections can create electrical resistance, excessive heat, intermittent operation, and potentially electrical arcing or damage to the devices. We explained why upgrading these devices to properly secured connections can help improve long-term reliability and reduce the potential for overheating.

Smoke & Carbon Monoxide Detection

We discussed adding an additional smoke detector for the downstairs bedroom to provide appropriate detection and notification in that sleeping area. We also reviewed the option of upgrading the existing smoke detectors to newer 10-year sealed-battery models. These units eliminate the need for routine battery replacements every couple of years and provide a convenient long-term solution for maintaining smoke detection throughout the home.

The homeowner stated that they are comfortable handling the GFCI replacements, exterior receptacles, back-stabbed device replacements, and smoke detector improvements themselves at this time.

Electrical Panel Replacement – 200-Amp GE Panel

LPH discussed the age of the existing 200-amp GE electrical panel, which is approximately 41 years old. Although the panel currently shows no visible rust or corrosion, it has exceeded the typical recommended service life of approximately 25–40 years.

We explained how internal breaker components, bus connections, and connection points experience wear over time. Aging components can contribute to loose connections, inconsistent breaker operation, overheating, and potential electrical arcing. LPH provided an estimate to replace the existing panel with a new premium Eaton CH panel, including updated breakers and whole-home surge protection.

Complete 200-Amp Electrical Service Replacement – LPH Preferred Recommendation

LPH also provided an estimate for a complete 200-amp electrical service replacement. During our evaluation, we identified evidence of long-term moisture intrusion within the existing exterior meter base. The back of the enclosure was never properly sealed, allowing moisture to enter over the years and create a damp environment. Corrosion is now becoming noticeable around the meter connection points and lugs, with additional rust developing on the mounting screws.

Although the existing service cables remain largely unaffected at this time, corrosion around electrical connection points can compromise connection integrity and contribute to overheating.

Our preferred long-term recommendation is to replace the entire electrical service rather than just the interior panel. This option includes a new exterior meter base, service entrance wiring, updated grounding and bonding, a new premium Eaton CH interior panel, and whole-home surge protection. This provides the homeowner with a more comprehensive solution by addressing both the age of the interior panel and the moisture-related deterioration developing in the exterior equipment.

Whole-Home Surge Protection

We also explained the importance of whole-home surge protection in today’s homes. Modern appliances and equipment contain sensitive electronic control boards that can be affected by voltage fluctuations and transient surges. These can originate from outside utility disturbances, lightning-related events, and even the everyday operation of larger appliances within the home. Whole-home surge protection helps limit damaging excess voltage and provides an additional layer of protection for the home’s electrical equipment.

Upstairs Bedroom Ceiling Fan & Lighting

LPH provided an additional estimate to install a ceiling fan with an integrated light in the upstairs bedroom. The current setup does not provide a convenient switched light when entering the room, requiring the homeowner to walk across the room in the dark to operate a lamp.

The proposed installation includes fishing new wiring through the attic, installing a properly rated ceiling fan support box, installing the homeowner-supplied fan, and fishing wiring down the existing wall to an existing switch location. This will provide convenient lighting and ceiling fan operation upon entering the bedroom.

Homeowner Decisions & Follow-Up

All findings and recommendations were reviewed with the homeowner, including the benefits of addressing the electrical safety concerns and completing the recommended upgrades. The homeowner indicated that they are comfortable handling the GFCI protection, exterior receptacle improvements, back-stabbed device replacements, and smoke detector upgrades independently.

At this time, the homeowner is not looking to move forward with the additional electrical maintenance or upgrades. However, they would like to receive the estimates for the interior panel replacement, complete 200-amp service replacement, and upstairs bedroom ceiling fan installation for consideration in the future.

Over time, the internal components of a panel experience normal wear and tear. Breaker contacts, bus connections, and internal connection points can deteriorate or lose their original tension. This can affect how reliably breakers operate, how securely electrical connections are maintained, and how effectively the panel distributes electricity throughout the home.

As these components age, the potential for loose connections, overheating, inconsistent breaker operation, and electrical arcing increases. Arcing can generate excessive heat and create a potential fire hazard, even when there are no obvious warning signs from outside the panel. Additionally, today’s homes place greater demands on electrical systems with the increased use of electronics, appliances, and modern equipment.

Replacing the existing panel allows LPH to provide the home with updated electrical distribution equipment, new breakers, and refreshed connections, helping improve the overall safety, reliability, and capacity of the home’s electrical system for years to come.

Whole-Home Surge Protection

As part of the panel replacement, LPH will install whole-home surge protection to meet current electrical code requirements.

Today’s homes contain more sensitive electronics and electrical equipment than ever before. Appliances such as refrigerators, washers, dryers, HVAC systems, microwaves, televisions, computers, and other modern devices rely on electronic control boards and sensitive components.

Not all damaging voltage surges come from lightning or outside utility problems. Everyday operation of equipment throughout the home, such as air conditioning systems, refrigerators, and other larger appliances, can create small voltage fluctuations known as transient surges. Over time, these repeated surges can contribute to premature wear or damage to sensitive electronics.

Whole-home surge protection provides an additional layer of defense by monitoring incoming electrical power and helping divert damaging excess voltage away from the home’s electrical system. This helps protect connected equipment from both externally introduced surges and internally generated voltage spikes.
e.438902522:
LPH Preferred Recommendation – Complete 200-Amp Electrical Service Replacement

Although replacing the interior electrical panel alone would address the age of the existing 41-year-old GE panel, LPH’s preferred recommendation is to replace the entire 200-amp electrical service, including both the interior panel and exterior service equipment.

During our evaluation, we identified evidence of long-term moisture intrusion at the existing exterior meter base. The back of the meter base was never properly sealed, allowing outside moisture to enter over the years and create a consistently damp environment within the enclosure. Although the existing service cables remain largely unaffected at this time, noticeable corrosion has begun developing around the meter connection points and lugs. Additionally, the mounting screws are showing signs of rust and deterioration.

While the service is currently operational, corrosion around electrical connection points can compromise connection integrity, increase electrical resistance, and contribute to excessive heat buildup. LPH does not recommend investing in a new interior panel while leaving aging, moisture-affected exterior service equipment in place.

With this preferred option, LPH will replace the complete 200-amp electrical service, including:

* New 200-amp exterior meter base.
* New exterior service entrance wiring and associated connections.
* Emergency exterior disconnect to code, adjusting the grounding to be moved to this location.
* New interior electrical panel utilizing the premium Eaton CH platform.
* New breakers and associated electrical connections.
* Updated grounding and bonding to meet current applicable electrical code requirements.
* Whole-home surge protection to help protect sensitive electronics and appliances from damaging transient voltage.
* All necessary permits, inspections, and utility coordination.

Premium Equipment & Long-Term Protection

LPH prioritizes using high-quality electrical equipment with strong manufacturer support and extended warranty coverage. We utilize the Eaton CH panel platform for its premium construction, dependable breaker technology, and excellent manufacturer warranty protection.

Whole-home surge protection will also be installed as part of the new service. Today’s homes contain increasingly sensitive electronics within HVAC systems, refrigerators, washers, dryers, televisions, computers, and other everyday appliances. Voltage surges can originate from utility disturbances, lightning-related events, and even the normal operation of larger appliances within the home. This additional layer of protection helps limit damaging transient voltage before it reaches sensitive equipment.

Why LPH Recommends Replacing the Entire Service

This option addresses both major concerns identified during today’s evaluation: the age of the interior electrical panel and the moisture-related deterioration developing within the exterior meter base.

Rather than replacing one portion of the system and retaining aging equipment elsewhere, LPH recommends taking care of the entire service together. This provides the homeowner with updated electrical distribution equipment, properly sealed exterior components, refreshed electrical connections, updated grounding and bonding, and modern surge protection.

Although the complete replacement is a larger investment upfront, it is the most comprehensive solution and provides the homeowner with the greatest long-term benefit. It eliminates the existing moisture-related concerns at the exterior service while addressing the age of the interior panel, helping reduce the likelihood of needing separate service-related replacements down the road.

LPH’s professional recommendation is to proceed with the complete 200-amp service replacement as the preferred long-term investment in the home’s electrical safety, reliability, and protection.

LPH originally arrived today to address an issue with the hot tub control button responsible for turning on the jets. We were able to quickly identify and correct the issue, restoring proper operation of the button. As an added value to the homeowner, and in appreciation of the additional electrical work approved during today’s visit, LPH completed this small repair at no additional charge.

After reviewing the additional recommendations and receiving approval from the homeowner, LPH completed the following work:

Smoke Detector Replacements:

LPH installed four new 10-year sealed lithium battery smoke detectors throughout the home. Additionally, one existing hardwired smoke detector was replaced with a new hardwired smoke detector equipped with battery backup. One hardwired combination smoke and carbon monoxide detector with battery backup was also installed. These replacements provide updated detection equipment and reliable early-warning protection in the event of a fire or carbon monoxide emergency.

Master Bathroom Exhaust Fan Replacement:

LPH removed and replaced the existing exhaust fan in the master bathroom. The original fan was noticeably noisy, and the motor had begun making a knocking sound, indicating signs of mechanical wear. The new fan was installed to restore proper ventilation, reduce operating noise, and help remove excess moisture from the bathroom.

New Bedroom Receptacle Installation:

LPH removed the existing device box in the hallway and utilized the opening to access the existing wiring. An additional wire was installed from the existing electrical box through the wall to a new location on the opposite side, inside the bedroom. A new cut-in electrical box and standard duplex receptacle were installed at the new location. All electrical connections were properly secured, and the new receptacle was tested to verify proper operation.

All approved work was completed, and the newly installed devices and equipment were tested and verified to be functioning properly prior to leaving. The hot tub jet control button was also repaired and verified to be operating properly at no additional charge.

Today’s invoice summary will be emailed to the homeowner for their records.

Thank you for allowing LPH into your home. It was a pleasure working with you, and we look forward to servicing you again in the future!

i.438814646:
Homeowner mentioned that there was no hot water coming out of the kitchen faucet. Technician removed the cover from the Noritz tankless water heater and connected a hose to the hot-water outlet service port to verify that the unit was firing and producing a flame at the heat exchanger. Technician cleaned the flame rod and igniter rod and noticed an improvement in the flame after cleaning. Technician then checked the hot-water temperature at the kitchen sink and recorded a temperature of 122°F, confirming that the unit was producing hot water.

Technician explained to the homeowner why it takes additional time for hot water to reach the kitchen sink. Technician also showed the homeowner the water distribution manifold and explained the hot-water piping layout and the path the water travels from the tankless water heater to the kitchen faucet.

Technician recommends scheduling routine maintenance on the Noritz tankless water heater. Routine maintenance includes flushing the heat exchanger to help remove mineral buildup, cleaning the flame rods, inspecting and cleaning the air intake screen, and cleaning the cold-water inlet filter. Regular maintenance helps maintain proper operation, improve efficiency, and extend the service life of the tankless water heater.

e.438849219: Technician performed routine maintenance on the tankless water heater. Technician flushed and descaled the heat exchanger to remove mineral buildup and help maintain optimal efficiency and performance. The flame rods were removed and cleaned to ensure proper flame sensing and reliable operation. Technician also cleaned the fresh air intake screen and cold water inlet screen to promote proper airflow and water flow through the unit. After maintenance was completed, the water heater was tested for proper operation. Unit was operating normally at the time of service and was left in good working condition.
